current_formulation: Three named graphs (assertion, provenance, publication info) with trusty URIs as the integrity key.

steps.formulation: Richly annotated statements carry context and provenance and are the unit of publication.
steps.quote: richly annotated RDF statements as carriers of unambiguous, meta-analyzed information in the form of traceable nano-publications

steps.formulation: A nanopublication is a set of annotations on one uniquely identified statement, each statement its own named graph.
steps.quote: Each statement is a separate Named Graph.

criticism.quote: Requiring formal representations for scientific results seems to be unrealistic in many cases

steps.formulation: Informal assertions as English sentences in the AIDA scheme.
steps.quote: we propose to allow authors to attach English sentences to nanopublications

criticism.quote: Published nanopublications are supposed to be immutable, but the current web has no mechanism to enforce this

steps.formulation: Trusty URIs: a cryptographic hash of the content inside the URI.
steps.quote: we propose a technique to include cryptographic hash values in URIs

steps.formulation: Three-graph guidelines: assertion, provenance, publication info, with trusty URIs recommended. The page is undated; the record date is the retrieval date.
steps.quote: MUST contain a link to the assertion graph identifier
